variant: Research version: carry the same character with trained LoRA weights instead of reference tokens. Phase 1 (experiment B0) builds the training dataset; no film is rendered from this version yet.
title: Night Elf Hunter — a boy and his bear crossing the grassland
status: research — B0 partial pass 2026-09-26: 30 images, identity 30/30, angles skewed (back 1/3, over-shoulder 0/2); v1 remains the delivered film
source: projects/nightelf_hunter/v1-drawthings-cli/seed/hunter.png — v1's adult master, itself edited from raw/kyle_ship.jpg
notes: This version exists to answer the B-series experiments in wiki/blueprint-v2-research.md, not to make a second film. v1 stays the delivered cut. The dataset deliberately breaks v1's practice in one place: v1 prompts name every feature to preserve, while these CAPTIONS name only what varies, so the permanent features bind to the trigger token nelf_kyle (the Isolation Rule). The generation prompts still name everything — two different strings per image, one to make the pixels and one to train on.

still.control: edit mode: --image seed/hunter.png --strength 1.0, one seed per cell (1..30)

post.upscale: none — training images stay at native size

dataset.experiment: B0 — can we build a LoRA dataset at all?
dataset.subject: half-elf hunter
dataset.split: 12 close-up / 12 medium / 6 wide — the 40/40/20 split in the source

axes.angle: front, three-quarter, side profile, back, over-shoulder, low, high
axes.light: studio, overcast, golden hour, hard noon, open shade, firelight, rim, window, storm, moonlight
axes.expression: neutral, faint smile, focused, alert, weary, laughing, frowning, speaking, eyes closed
axes.wardrobe: armour, hood up, no cloak, linen tunic, fur cloak, bare shoulders, rain-soaked
axes.background: grey studio, grassland, forest, night camp, city street, river bank, stone hall

dataset.keep_clause: exactly the same face and the same identity — the same East Asian features, the same strong jaw and light stubble, the same age of about twenty-eight, the same straight jet-black side-parted hair, the same long slender pointed ears, the same faint pale blue-green markings curving under each eye
dataset.caption_rule: trigger, framing, angle, wardrobe, background, light, expression. Face, ears, markings, hair and age are omitted on purpose — captioned features stay steerable, uncaptioned ones bind to the trigger.

hyperparameters_for_B1.note: unverified — from the source deep-dive, not measured here

result.wall_time: 13 min for 30 + 10 min re-rendering 17 cells, ~26 s per image
result.identity: recognisable in 30/30; no two-face artifact in 5 profile cells; ds_19 hair drifted brown on the first pass and cleared on re-render
result.honoured: lighting 10/10, background 7/7, wardrobe 7/7, expression 9/9, framing after switching the canvas per framing (close 512x768, medium 512x512, wide 768x512)
result.refused: back 1/3, over-shoulder 0/2, camera height 2/4 — klein repaints anything, but recomposes the camera only as far as the canvas forces it, and will not hide a face it can see in the reference
result.blocker_for_B1: the set is skewed toward front and three-quarter faces, the angles reference tokens already cover, so B2 would measure dataset bias rather than method. Back and profile cells need a non-frontal source: real photos, or frames pulled from v1's clips.
